  11 |     | 
  12 |     | /// @notice Deploys the RWA tokenization stack to Base Sepolia and wires it, then
  13 |     | ///         seeds the compliant on-chain state the demo page reads: whitelists
  14 |     | ///         the deployer and Investor A, registers a batch of backing assets,
  15 |     | ///         pushes an oracle price, and mints fractions to Investor A.
  16 |     | /// @dev Reads the deployer key from `DEMO_DEPLOYER_PK` (env, never argv) and
  17 |     | ///      Investor A's address from `DEMO_INVESTOR_A_ADDR`. Refuses to run on any chain but
  18 |     | ///      Base Sepolia. The Investor-A-signed narrative txs (a successful
  19 |     | ///      transfer, the reverting transfer to the un-whitelisted Investor B, and a
  20 |     | ///      redemption) are executed afterward by scripts/seed-investor.sh, which
  21 |     | ///      holds Investor A's key.
  22 |     | contract Deploy is Script {
  23 |     |     uint256 internal constant BASE_SEPOLIA_CHAIN_ID = 84532;
  24 |     | 
  25 |     |     /// @notice Tokens minted to Investor A on deploy (10,000 whole tokens).
  26 |     |     uint256 internal constant SEED_MINT = 10_000 ether;
  27 |     |     /// @notice Seed oracle price, in USD cents per token (i.e. $1.05).
  28 |     |     uint256 internal constant SEED_PRICE_CENTS = 105;
  29 |     | 
  30 |     |     /// @notice The wrong-chain guard.
  31 |     |     error WrongChain(uint256 expected, uint256 actual);
  32 |     | 
  33 |     |     function run() external {
  34 |     |         if (block.chainid != BASE_SEPOLIA_CHAIN_ID) {
  35 |     |             revert WrongChain(BASE_SEPOLIA_CHAIN_ID, block.chainid);
  36 |     |         }
  37 |     | 
  38 |     |         // Unified role keys, shared by all three demo repos. See
  39 |     |         // pigfox2-repos/KEYS.md for the addresses and what each role may do.
  40 |     |         uint256 deployerKey = vm.envUint("DEMO_DEPLOYER_PK");
  41 |     |         address deployer = vm.addr(deployerKey);
  42 |     |         address investorA = vm.envAddress("DEMO_INVESTOR_A_ADDR");
  43 |     | 
  44 |     |         vm.startBroadcast(deployerKey);
  45 |     | 
  46 |     |         // Deploy.
  47 |     |         IdentityRegistry identity = new IdentityRegistry(deployer);
  48 |     |         AssetRegistry assets = new AssetRegistry(deployer);
  49 |     |         PriceOracle oracle = new PriceOracle(deployer);
  50 |     |         RWAToken token = new RWAToken("Acme Tower Fractions", "ACME", address(identity), deployer);
  51 |     |         Redemption redemption = new Redemption(address(token), address(assets), deployer);
  52 |     | 
  53 |     |         // Wire the compliance relationships.
  54 |     |         identity.setToken(address(token));
  55 |     |         token.setRedeemer(address(redemption));
  56 |     | 
  57 |     |         // Whitelist the two KYC-verified parties (deployer + Investor A). Investor
  58 |     |         // B is deliberately left un-whitelisted so the demo's transfer to it reverts.
  59 |     |         identity.registerIdentity(deployer);
  60 |     |         identity.registerIdentity(investorA);
  61 |     | 
  62 |     |         // Register the backing assets. Enough rows to page the "all assets" table.
  63 |     |         string[12] memory uris = _assetUris();
  64 |     |         for (uint256 i = 0; i < uris.length; i++) {
  65 |     |             assets.registerAsset(keccak256(bytes(uris[i])), uris[i]);
  66 |     |         }
  67 |     | 
  68 |     |         // Seed the oracle and mint fractions to Investor A.
  69 |     |         oracle.setPrice(SEED_PRICE_CENTS);
  70 |     |         token.mint(investorA, SEED_MINT);
  71 |     | 
  72 |     |         vm.stopBroadcast();
  73 |     | 
  74 |     |         console2.log("IdentityRegistry:", address(identity));
  75 |     |         console2.log("AssetRegistry:   ", address(assets));
  76 |     |         console2.log("PriceOracle:     ", address(oracle));
  77 |     |         console2.log("RWAToken:        ", address(token));
  78 |     |         console2.log("Redemption:      ", address(redemption));
  79 |     |         console2.log("Deployer:        ", deployer);
  80 |     |         console2.log("Investor A:      ", investorA);
  81 |     |     }
  82 |     | 
  83 |     |     /// @dev Realistic metadata URIs for the seeded assets. The document hash of
  84 |     |     ///      each is the keccak of its URI, so the seed is fully deterministic.
  85 |     |     function _assetUris() internal pure returns (string[12] memory uris) {
  86 |     |         uris[0] = "ipfs://bafy-acme-tower-manhattan-office-deed";

  88 |     |         uris[2] = "ipfs://bafy-solar-farm-nevada-ppa-bundle";
  89 |     |         uris[3] = "ipfs://bafy-vineyard-estate-napa-land-grant";
  90 |     |         uris[4] = "ipfs://bafy-marina-berths-portfolio-lease";
  91 |     |         uris[5] = "ipfs://bafy-datacenter-ashburn-colocation-note";
  92 |     |         uris[6] = "ipfs://bafy-timberland-oregon-parcel-registry";

  94 |     |         uris[8] = "ipfs://bafy-wind-portfolio-texas-turbine-set";

   4 |     | import {Roles} from "./Roles.sol";

   7 |     | /// @title AssetRegistry
   8 |     | /// @notice Registrar-only attestation of the off-chain real-world assets that
   9 |     | ///         back the token. Each asset records a document hash, a metadata URI,
  10 |     | ///         and a lifecycle status. Ids are assigned sequentially from zero, so
  11 |     | ///         `assetCount` doubles as a cheap total for window-driven pagination.
  12 | *   | contract AssetRegistry is Roles, IAssetRegistry {
  13 |     |     /*//////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
  14 |     |                                   TYPES
  15 |     |     //////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////*/
  16 |     | 
  17 |     |     /// @notice Lifecycle status of a registered asset.
  18 |     |     /// @dev `None` is the zero value and means "not registered".
  19 |     |     enum Status {
  20 |     |         None,
  21 |     |         Active,
  22 |     |         Suspended,
  23 |     |         Redeemed
  24 |     |     }
  25 |     | 
  26 |     |     /// @notice On-chain record attesting to an off-chain asset.
  27 |     |     struct Asset {
  28 |     |         bytes32 docHash;
  29 |     |         string uri;
  30 |     |         Status status;
  31 |     |         bool exists;
  32 |     |     }
  33 |     | 
  34 |     |     /*//////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
  35 |     |                                  ERRORS
  36 |     |     //////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////*/
  37 |     | 
  38 |     |     /// @notice No asset is registered under this id.
  39 |     |     error UnknownAsset(uint256 assetId);
  40 |     |     /// @notice A status update tried to set the zero (`None`) status.
  41 |     |     error InvalidStatus();
  42 |     | 
  43 |     |     /*//////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
  44 |     |                                  EVENTS
  45 |     |     //////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////*/
  46 |     | 
  47 |     |     /// @notice Emitted when a new asset is registered.
  48 |     |     /// @param assetId The sequential id assigned to the asset; ids are never reused.
  49 |     |     /// @param docHash Hash of the off-chain document backing the asset. The document itself
  50 |     |     ///        stays off chain; only its hash is attested, so the record proves which
  51 |     |     ///        document was meant without publishing its contents.
  52 |     |     /// @param uri Where that document can be fetched.
  53 |     |     event AssetRegistered(uint256 indexed assetId, bytes32 docHash, string uri);
  54 |     |     /// @notice Emitted when an asset's status changes.
  55 |     |     /// @param assetId The asset whose lifecycle state changed.
  56 |     |     /// @param previousStatus The status before the change, emitted so the log alone is a
  57 |     |     ///        complete lifecycle history without replaying prior events.
  58 |     |     /// @param newStatus The status after the change. Never `None`, which is reserved for
  59 |     |     ///        "no such asset".
  60 |     |     event AssetStatusUpdated(uint256 indexed assetId, Status previousStatus, Status newStatus);
  61 |     | 
  62 |     |     /*//////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
  63 |     |                                  STORAGE
  64 |     |     //////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////*/
  65 |     | 
  66 |     |     mapping(uint256 assetId => Asset asset) private _assets;
  67 |     |     /// @notice Number of assets registered; also the id the next registration
  68 |     |     ///         will use. Enables O(perPage) pagination over the asset list.
  69 | *   |     uint256 public assetCount;
  70 |     | 
  71 |     |     /// @notice Deploys an empty asset registry.
  72 |     |     /// @param initialOwner The deployer; owner and first (registrar) agent.
  73 | *   |     constructor(address initialOwner) Roles(initialOwner) {}
  74 |     | 
  75 |     |     /*//////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
  76 |     |                                 REGISTRAR
  77 |     |     //////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////*/
  78 |     | 
  79 |     |     /// @notice Register a new asset with `docHash` and metadata `uri`. Starts Active.
  80 |     |     /// @param docHash Hash of the backing document. Not validated against zero: this
  81 |     |     ///        registry attests what the registrar supplied and does not pretend to judge
  82 |     |     ///        whether the document exists.
  83 |     |     /// @param uri Where the document can be fetched.
  84 |     |     /// @return assetId The sequential id assigned to the new asset.
  85 | *   |     function registerAsset(bytes32 docHash, string calldata uri)
  86 |     |         external
  87 |     |         onlyAgent
  88 | *   |         returns (uint256 assetId)
  89 |     |     {
  90 | *   |         assetId = assetCount;
  91 | *   |         _assets[assetId] = Asset({docHash: docHash, uri: uri, status: Status.Active, exists: true});
  92 | *   |         assetCount = assetId + 1;
  93 | *   |         emit AssetRegistered(assetId, docHash, uri);
  94 |     |     }
  95 |     | 
  96 |     |     /// @notice Change the status of a registered asset. Cannot set `None`.
  97 |     |     /// @param assetId The asset to update. Reverts with `UnknownAsset` if never registered.
  98 |     |     /// @param newStatus The status to move to. `None` is rejected because it is the zero
  99 |     |     ///        value meaning "no such asset" — allowing it would let a registrar erase an
 100 |     |     ///        asset's existence rather than mark it inactive.
 101 |     |     function setAssetStatus(uint256 assetId, Status newStatus) external onlyAgent {
 102 |     |         Asset storage a = _assets[assetId];
 103 |     |         if (!a.exists) revert UnknownAsset(assetId);
 104 |     |         if (newStatus == Status.None) revert InvalidStatus();
 105 |     |         Status previous = a.status;
 106 |     |         a.status = newStatus;
 107 |     |         emit AssetStatusUpdated(assetId, previous, newStatus);
 108 |     |     }
 109 |     | 
 110 |     |     /*//////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
 111 |     |                                   VIEWS
 112 |     |     //////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////*/
 113 |     | 
 114 |     |     /// @notice The full record for `assetId`. Reverts if unknown.
 115 |     |     /// @param assetId The asset to read.
 116 |     |     /// @return The document hash, metadata URI, status and existence flag. Reverts rather
 117 |     |     ///         than returning a zeroed struct, so an unknown id cannot be read as a real
 118 |     |     ///         asset with an empty document.
 119 |     |     function getAsset(uint256 assetId) external view returns (Asset memory) {
 120 |     |         Asset storage a = _assets[assetId];
 121 |     |         if (!a.exists) revert UnknownAsset(assetId);
 122 |     |         return a;
 123 |     |     }
 124 |     | 
 125 |     |     /// @notice True when `assetId` exists and its status is Active.
 126 |     |     /// @param assetId The asset to test.
 127 |     |     /// @return True only when the asset both exists and is Active. An unknown id returns
 128 |     |     ///         false rather than reverting, because redemption asks this as a yes/no
 129 |     |     ///         eligibility question, not as a lookup.
 130 | *   |     function isActive(uint256 assetId) external view override returns (bool) {
 131 | *   |         Asset storage a = _assets[assetId];
 132 | *   |         return a.exists && a.status == Status.Active;
 133 |     |     }
 134 |     | }

   1 |     | // SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

   4 |     | import {Roles} from "./Roles.sol";

   7 |     | 
   8 |     | /// @title IdentityRegistry
   9 |     | /// @notice KYC whitelist for the RWA token. Agents register and remove
  10 |     | ///         verified identities; the token consults {isVerified} on every mint
  11 |     | ///         and transfer.
  12 |     | /// @dev A bound token (see {setToken}) makes the security invariant
  13 |     | ///      "a non-verified address can never hold a non-zero balance" hold even
  14 |     | ///      across de-verification: an identity that currently holds tokens cannot
  15 |     | ///      be removed. Acquisition is already gated by the token's mint/transfer
  16 |     | ///      hooks, so the only remaining escape — de-verifying a live holder — is
  17 |     | ///      closed here.
  18 | *   | contract IdentityRegistry is Roles, IIdentityRegistry {
  19 |     |     /*//////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
  20 |     |                                  ERRORS
  21 |     |     //////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////*/
  22 |     | 
  23 |     |     /// @notice The identity is already verified.
  24 |     |     error AlreadyVerified(address account);
  25 |     |     /// @notice The identity is not currently verified.
  26 |     |     error NotVerifiedIdentity(address account);
  27 |     |     /// @notice The identity still holds tokens and so cannot be removed.
  28 |     |     error HolderHasBalance(address account, uint256 balance);
  29 |     |     /// @notice The bound token has already been set and is immutable thereafter.
  30 |     |     error TokenAlreadySet();
  31 |     | 
  32 |     |     /*//////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
  33 |     |                                  EVENTS
  34 |     |     //////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////*/
  35 |     | 
  36 |     |     /// @notice Emitted when `account` becomes a verified identity.
  37 |     |     /// @param account The address added to the whitelist.
  38 |     |     event IdentityRegistered(address indexed account);
  39 |     |     /// @notice Emitted when `account` is removed from the whitelist.
  40 |     |     /// @param account The address removed. It necessarily held a zero balance at this
  41 |     |     ///        point, because `removeIdentity` refuses to strip a holder.
  42 |     |     event IdentityRemoved(address indexed account);
  43 |     |     /// @notice Emitted once when the bound token is configured.
  44 |     |     /// @param token The token whose balances now guard de-verification. Emitted at most
  45 |     |     ///        once in this contract's lifetime — `setToken` is one-shot.
  46 |     |     event TokenSet(address indexed token);
  47 |     | 
  48 |     |     /*//////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
  49 |     |                                  STORAGE
  50 |     |     //////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////*/
  51 |     | 
  52 |     |     mapping(address account => bool verified) private _verified;
  53 |     |     /// @notice The token whose balances gate de-verification. Set once, post-deploy.
  54 |     |     IRWAToken public token;
  55 |     | 
  56 |     |     /// @notice Deploys the whitelist with no token bound and nobody verified.
  57 |     |     /// @param initialOwner The deployer; owner and first agent.
  58 | *   |     constructor(address initialOwner) Roles(initialOwner) {}
  59 |     | 
  60 |     |     /*//////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
  61 |     |                                  WIRING
  62 |     |     //////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////*/
  63 |     | 
  64 |     |     /// @notice Bind the token whose balances guard de-verification. One-shot:
  65 |     |     ///         reverts once set, so the guard cannot later be disabled.
  66 |     |     /// @param token_ The RWA token to bind. Rejected if zero, and rejected outright if a
  67 |     |     ///        token is already bound: re-pointing it would let an owner swap in a token
  68 |     |     ///        with no balances and then de-verify a holder who still owns the real one,
  69 |     |     ///        which is precisely the invariant this binding exists to protect.
  70 | *   |     function setToken(address token_) external onlyOwner {
  71 | *   |         if (token_ == address(0)) revert ZeroAddress();
  72 | *   |         if (address(token) != address(0)) revert TokenAlreadySet();
  73 | *   |         token = IRWAToken(token_);
  74 | *   |         emit TokenSet(token_);
  75 |     |     }
  76 |     | 
  77 |     |     /*//////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
  78 |     |                                 WHITELIST
  79 |     |     //////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////*/
  80 |     | 
  81 |     |     /// @notice Add `account` to the KYC whitelist.
  82 |     |     /// @param account The address to verify. Rejected if zero, and rejected if already
  83 |     |     ///        verified — a redundant re-registration is treated as a mistake worth
  84 |     |     ///        surfacing rather than a silent no-op.
  85 | *   |     function registerIdentity(address account) external onlyAgent {
  86 | *   |         if (account == address(0)) revert ZeroAddress();
  87 | *   |         if (_verified[account]) revert AlreadyVerified(account);
  88 | *   |         _verified[account] = true;
  89 | *   |         emit IdentityRegistered(account);
  90 |     |     }
  91 |     | 
  92 |     |     /// @notice Remove `account` from the KYC whitelist.
  93 |     |     /// @dev Reverts if a token is bound and `account` still holds a balance,
  94 |     |     ///      preserving the non-verified-cannot-hold invariant.
  95 |     |     /// @param account The address to de-verify. Reverts with `HolderHasBalance` if a token
  96 |     |     ///        is bound and the account still holds one, so de-verification can never
  97 |     |     ///        strand tokens in an address that is no longer allowed to move them.
  98 |     |     function removeIdentity(address account) external onlyAgent {
  99 |     |         if (!_verified[account]) revert NotVerifiedIdentity(account);
 100 |     |         if (address(token) != address(0)) {
 101 |     |             uint256 bal = token.balanceOf(account);
 102 |     |             if (bal > 0) revert HolderHasBalance(account, bal);
 103 |     |         }
 104 |     |         _verified[account] = false;
 105 |     |         emit IdentityRemoved(account);
 106 |     |     }
 107 |     | 
 108 |     |     /*//////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
 109 |     |                                   VIEWS
 110 |     |     //////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////*/
 111 |     | 
 112 |     |     /// @notice True when `account` is a KYC-verified identity permitted to hold
 113 |     |     ///         and transact the token. Consulted by the token on every mint and
 114 |     |     ///         transfer.
 115 |     |     /// @param account The address to test.
 116 |     |     /// @return True while the address is whitelisted. A plain list membership test — unlike
 117 |     |     ///         zk-kyc-pass's registry there is no expiry, so verification persists until an
 118 |     |     ///         agent removes it.
 119 | *   |     function isVerified(address account) external view override returns (bool) {
 120 | *   |         return _verified[account];
 121 |     |     }
 122 |     | }

  1 |     | // SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

  5 |     |

  9 |     | ///         timestamp so consumers can reason about staleness.
 10 |     | /// @dev `updatedAt` is monotonically non-decreasing: it is only ever assigned
 11 |     | ///      `block.timestamp`, which never moves backwards between transactions.
 12 | *   | contract PriceOracle is Roles {
 13 |     |     /*//////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
 14 |     |                                  ERRORS
 15 |     |     //////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////*/
 16 |     | 
 17 |     |     /// @notice No price has been pushed yet, so the query is undefined.
 18 |     |     error NoPrice();
 19 |     | 
 20 |     |     /*//////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
 21 |     |                                  EVENTS
 22 |     |     //////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////*/
 23 |     | 
 24 |     |     /// @notice Emitted on every price push.
 25 |     |     /// @param price The pushed price, in the oracle's own unit.
 26 |     |     /// @param updatedAt The block timestamp stamped onto the push. Emitted on every call,
 27 |     |     ///        including one that pushes an unchanged price, so a consumer can distinguish
 28 |     |     ///        "the price is still this" from "nobody has updated it".
 29 |     |     event PriceUpdated(uint256 price, uint256 updatedAt);
 30 |     | 
 31 |     |     /*//////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
 32 |     |                                  STORAGE
 33 |     |     //////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////*/
 34 |     | 
 35 |     |     /// @notice Latest pushed price, in the oracle's own unit (e.g. USD cents per token).
 36 |     |     uint256 public price;
 37 |     |     /// @notice Block timestamp of the latest push. Zero until the first update.
 38 | *   |     uint256 public updatedAt;
 39 |     | 
 40 |     |     /// @notice Deploys the oracle with no price yet published.
 41 |     |     /// @param initialOwner The deployer; owner and first (updater) agent.
 42 | *   |     constructor(address initialOwner) Roles(initialOwner) {}
 43 |     | 
 44 |     |     /*//////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
 45 |     |                                  UPDATER
 46 |     |     //////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////*/
 47 |     | 
 48 |     |     /// @notice Push a new price. Stamps `updatedAt` with the current block time.
 49 |     |     /// @param newPrice The price to publish. Zero is accepted deliberately: this is a mock
 50 |     |     ///        push oracle, and rejecting zero would make "the asset is worthless" the one
 51 |     |     ///        state it could not report.
 52 | *   |     function setPrice(uint256 newPrice) external onlyAgent {
 53 | *   |         price = newPrice;
 54 | *   |         updatedAt = block.timestamp;
 55 | *   |         emit PriceUpdated(newPrice, block.timestamp);
 56 |     |     }
 57 |     | 
 58 |     |     /*//////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
 59 |     |                                   VIEWS
 60 |     |     //////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////*/
 61 |     | 
 62 |     |     /// @notice The latest price and the timestamp it was pushed. Reverts if
 63 |     |     ///         no price has ever been set.
 64 |     |     /// @return currentPrice The latest pushed price.
 65 |     |     /// @return at The timestamp it was pushed, so the caller can judge staleness itself
 66 |     |     ///         rather than trusting the oracle's own verdict.
 67 |     |     function latestPrice() external view returns (uint256 currentPrice, uint256 at) {
 68 |     |         if (updatedAt == 0) revert NoPrice();
 69 |     |         return (price, updatedAt);
 70 |     |     }
 71 |     | 
 72 |     |     /// @notice True when the latest price is older than `maxAge` seconds.
 73 |     |     /// @dev Reverts if no price has ever been pushed; staleness is undefined then.
 74 |     |     /// @param maxAge The oldest age in seconds still considered fresh. Compared with a
 75 |     |     ///        strict `>`, so a price exactly `maxAge` old is still fresh.
 76 |     |     /// @return True when the latest push is older than `maxAge`.
 77 |     |     function isStale(uint256 maxAge) external view returns (bool) {
 78 |     |         if (updatedAt == 0) revert NoPrice();
 79 |     |         return block.timestamp - updatedAt > maxAge;
 80 |     |     }
 81 |     | }

   8 |     | /// @title Redemption
   9 |     | /// @notice Lets a holder burn tokens against a registered, active asset in
  10 |     | ///         exchange for an off-chain settlement. A request records who redeemed
  11 |     | ///         how much of which asset; an admin agent later marks it settled once
  12 |     | ///         the off-chain leg completes. Requests are sequential from zero, so
  13 |     | ///         `requestCount` is a cheap total for window-driven pagination.
  14 | *   | contract Redemption is Roles {
  15 |     |     /*//////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
  16 |     |                                  ERRORS
  17 |     |     //////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////*/
  18 |     | 
  19 |     |     /// @notice The asset is not registered or not currently active.
  20 |     |     error AssetNotActive(uint256 assetId);
  21 |     |     /// @notice A redemption for zero tokens was requested.
  22 |     |     error ZeroAmount();
  23 |     |     /// @notice No request exists under this id.
  24 |     |     error UnknownRequest(uint256 requestId);
  25 |     |     /// @notice The request was already settled.
  26 |     |     error AlreadySettled(uint256 requestId);
  27 |     | 
  28 |     |     /*//////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
  29 |     |                                  EVENTS
  30 |     |     //////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////*/
  31 |     | 
  32 |     |     /// @notice Emitted when a holder burns tokens to request redemption.
  33 |     |     /// @param requestId The sequential id assigned to the request; ids are never reused.
  34 |     |     /// @param holder The redeeming account. Always `msg.sender` — there is no path by
  35 |     |     ///        which one account can redeem another's holding.
  36 |     |     /// @param assetId The asset redeemed against, which was Active at this moment.
  37 |     |     /// @param amount The tokens burned. Emitted BEFORE the burn under strict CEI; if the
  38 |     |     ///        burn reverts the whole call reverts and this event is never observed.
  39 |     |     event RedemptionRequested(
  40 |     |         uint256 indexed requestId, address indexed holder, uint256 indexed assetId, uint256 amount
  41 |     |     );
  42 |     |     /// @notice Emitted when an admin settles a redemption request.
  43 |     |     /// @param requestId The request marked settled. Settlement is the on-chain record that
  44 |     |     ///        the off-chain leg completed; it moves no tokens, because the tokens were
  45 |     |     ///        already burned when the request was made.
  46 |     |     event RedemptionSettled(uint256 indexed requestId);

  48 |     |     /*//////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////

  53 |     |     struct Request {

  71 |     |     /// @notice Number of redemption requests recorded; also the next request id.
  72 | *   |     uint256 public requestCount;

  74 |     |     /// @notice Binds redemption to the token it burns and the registry it checks.
  75 |     |     /// @dev Both are stored as `immutable`, so the token whose supply this contract can
  76 |     |     ///      destroy is fixed at deployment and cannot later be pointed at another.
  77 |     |     /// @param token_ The RWA token address (non-zero).
  78 |     |     /// @param assetRegistry_ The asset registry address (non-zero).
  79 |     |     /// @param initialOwner The deployer; owner and first (admin) agent.
  80 | *   |     constructor(address token_, address assetRegistry_, address initialOwner) Roles(initialOwner) {
  81 | *   |         if (token_ == address(0) || assetRegistry_ == address(0)) revert ZeroAddress();
  82 | *   |         token = IRWAToken(token_);
  83 | *   |         assetRegistry = IAssetRegistry(assetRegistry_);
  84 |     |     }
  85 |     | 
  86 |     |     /*//////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
  87 |     |                                 REDEEM

  89 |     | 
  90 |     |     /// @notice Burn `amount` of the caller's tokens against active `assetId` and
  91 |     |     ///         record a redemption request.
  92 |     |     /// @param assetId The asset to redeem against. Must be registered and Active; an
  93 |     |     ///        unknown or inactive id reverts before any token is burned.
  94 |     |     /// @param amount The tokens to burn. Zero is rejected, so a request always corresponds
  95 |     |     ///        to a real burn.
  96 |     |     /// @return requestId The sequential id assigned to the new request.
  97 | *   |     function requestRedemption(uint256 assetId, uint256 amount) external returns (uint256 requestId) {
  98 |     |         // Checks.
  99 | *   |         if (amount == 0) revert ZeroAmount();
 100 | *   |         if (!assetRegistry.isActive(assetId)) revert AssetNotActive(assetId);
 101 |     | 
 102 |     |         // Effects: record the request before the external burn (strict CEI). If
 103 |     |         // the burn reverts (caller lacks the balance) the whole call reverts and
 104 |     |         // this write is rolled back, so state can never diverge from the token.
 105 | *   |         requestId = requestCount;
 106 | *   |         _requests[requestId] =

/tmp/codex-phase32-rwa/src/Roles.sol
   1 |     | // SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
   2 |     | pragma solidity 0.8.28;
   3 |     | 
   4 |     | /// @title Roles
   5 |     | /// @notice Minimal two-tier access control shared by every contract in the RWA
   6 |     | ///         tokenization demo: a single `owner` (governance) and a set of
   7 |     | ///         `agents` (operational actors). This mirrors the owner/agent split of
   8 |     | ///         ERC-3643 (T-REX) without vendoring the full suite.
   9 |     | /// @dev The deployer is set as BOTH owner and the first agent in the
  10 |     | ///      constructor, so a freshly deployed contract is immediately operable by
  11 |     | ///      the deployer alone — which is exactly how this demo is wired: every
  12 |     | ///      privileged role resolves to the single deployer address.
  13 |     | abstract contract Roles {
  14 |     |     /*//////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
  15 |     |                                  ERRORS
  16 |     |     //////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////*/
  17 |     | 
  18 |     |     /// @notice The caller is not the owner.
  19 |     |     error NotOwner(address caller);
  20 |     |     /// @notice The caller does not hold the agent role.
  21 |     |     error NotAgent(address caller);
  22 |     |     /// @notice A zero address was supplied where a real account is required.
  23 |     |     error ZeroAddress();
  24 |     | 
  25 |     |     /*//////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
  26 |     |                                  EVENTS
  27 |     |     //////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////*/
  28 |     | 
  29 |     |     /// @notice Emitted when ownership moves from `previousOwner` to `newOwner`.
  30 |     |     /// @param previousOwner The outgoing owner. Zero on the constructor's emission, which
  31 |     |     ///        is what makes the deploy transaction itself the auditable origin of ownership.
  32 |     |     /// @param newOwner The incoming owner.
  33 |     |     event OwnershipTransferred(address indexed previousOwner, address indexed newOwner);
  34 |     |     /// @notice Emitted when `account` is granted (`enabled=true`) or revoked the agent role.
  35 |     |     /// @param account The account whose agent role changed.
  36 |     |     /// @param enabled True when the role was granted, false when revoked. Emitted on every
  37 |     |     ///        call, including a no-op re-grant, so the event log is a complete history of
  38 |     |     ///        intent rather than only of changes.
  39 |     |     event AgentSet(address indexed account, bool enabled);
  40 |     | 
  41 |     |     /*//////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
  42 |     |                                  STORAGE
  43 |     |     //////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////*/
  44 |     | 
  45 |     |     /// @notice The governance account. May transfer ownership and manage agents.
  46 | *   |     address public owner;
  47 |     |     /// @notice Operational actors permitted to take agent-gated actions.
  48 |     |     mapping(address account => bool isAgent) public agents;
  49 |     | 
  50 |     |     /*//////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
  51 |     |                                 MODIFIERS
  52 |     |     //////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////*/
  53 |     | 
  54 |     |     modifier onlyOwner() {
  55 | *   |         if (msg.sender != owner) revert NotOwner(msg.sender);
  56 |     |         _;
  57 |     |     }
  58 |     | 
  59 |     |     modifier onlyAgent() {
  60 | *   |         if (!agents[msg.sender]) revert NotAgent(msg.sender);
  61 |     |         _;
  62 |     |     }
  63 |     | 
  64 |     |     /*//////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
  65 |     |                                CONSTRUCTOR
  66 |     |     //////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////*/
  67 |     | 
  68 |     |     /// @notice Sets the deploying governance account as owner and first agent.
  69 |     |     /// @param initialOwner The account that becomes owner and the first agent. Rejected if
  70 |     |     ///        zero: a contract with no owner could never grant an agent, so the whole
  71 |     |     ///        agent-gated surface would be permanently unreachable.
  72 | *   |     constructor(address initialOwner) {
  73 | *   |         if (initialOwner == address(0)) revert ZeroAddress();
  74 | *   |         owner = initialOwner;
  75 | *   |         agents[initialOwner] = true;
  76 | *   |         emit OwnershipTransferred(address(0), initialOwner);
  77 | *   |         emit AgentSet(initialOwner, true);
  78 |     |     }
  79 |     | 
  80 |     |     /*//////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
  81 |     |                                GOVERNANCE
  82 |     |     //////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////*/
  83 |     | 
  84 |     |     /// @notice Transfer ownership to `newOwner`.
  85 |     |     /// @dev The new owner is NOT granted an agent role automatically; manage
  86 |     |     ///      that separately with {setAgent} if the new owner should also operate.
  87 |     |     /// @param newOwner The account to hand governance to. Rejected if zero — this contract
  88 |     |     ///        has no renounce path, so a zero transfer would be an irreversible mistake
  89 |     |     ///        rather than a deliberate abdication.
  90 |     |     function transferOwnership(address newOwner) external onlyOwner {
  91 |     |         if (newOwner == address(0)) revert ZeroAddress();
  92 |     |         emit OwnershipTransferred(owner, newOwner);
  93 |     |         owner = newOwner;
  94 |     |     }
  95 |     | 
  96 |     |     /// @notice Grant (`enabled=true`) or revoke the agent role for `account`.
  97 |     |     /// @param account The account to grant or revoke. Rejected if zero, so the agent
  98 |     |     ///        mapping can never record a role against the null address.
  99 |     |     /// @param enabled True to grant, false to revoke. Owner-only, and separate from
 100 |     |     ///        ownership: an agent operates, an owner governs.
 101 |     |     function setAgent(address account, bool enabled) external onlyOwner {
 102 |     |         if (account == address(0)) revert ZeroAddress();
 103 |     |         agents[account] = enabled;
 104 |     |         emit AgentSet(account, enabled);
 105 |     |     }
 106 |     | }

/tmp/codex-phase32-rwa/test/Actor.sol
  1 |     | // SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
  2 |     | pragma solidity 0.8.28;
  3 |     | 
  4 |     | /// @title Actor — a callable stand-in for a token holder.
  5 |     | /// @notice Echidna and Medusa have no cheatcodes, so a harness that needs a call
  6 |     | ///         to arrive from a specific `msg.sender` cannot prank one: it has to own
  7 |     | ///         a contract at that address and call through it. That is all this is.
  8 |     | ///
  9 |     | /// @dev    It matters here specifically because `Redemption.requestRedemption`
 10 |     | ///         records `msg.sender` as the holder and burns that account's tokens.
 11 |     | ///         Without distinct actors every redemption in a campaign would be the
 12 |     | ///         harness redeeming from itself, and the ledger invariants would only
 13 |     | ///         ever see one holder — which is exactly the shape of a bug they are
 14 |     | ///         meant to catch.
 15 | *   | contract Actor {
 16 |     |     /// @notice Forwards `data` to `target` and reports whether it succeeded.
 17 |     |     /// @dev Returns the outcome rather than bubbling the revert. The harness
 18 |     |     ///      compares outcomes against what it expected; a bubbled revert would
 19 |     |     ///      abort the fuzzer's transaction instead, which turns an interesting
 20 |     |     ///      state into a discarded one.
 21 | *   |     function call(address target, bytes calldata data) external returns (bool ok, bytes memory ret) {
 22 |     |         // solhint-disable-next-line avoid-low-level-calls
 23 | *   |         (ok, ret) = target.call(data);
 24 |     |     }
 25 |     | }
 26 |     |

/tmp/codex-phase32-rwa/test/Invariants.t.sol
   1 |     | // SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
   2 |     | pragma solidity 0.8.28;
   3 |     | 
   4 |     | import {Test} from "forge-std/Test.sol";
   5 |     | import {Properties} from "./Properties.sol";
   6 |     | 
   7 |     | /// @title InvariantsTest — the third engine on the same property file.
   8 |     | /// @notice Echidna and Medusa both drive `test/Properties.sol`. So does Foundry's
   9 |     | ///         invariant runner, here. Three engines, ONE set of predicates: a
  10 |     | ///         property cannot hold under one and quietly rot under another, and a
  11 |     | ///         plain `forge test` catches a broken invariant before anyone reaches
  12 |     | ///         for a fuzzer.
  13 |     | ///
  14 |     | /// @dev    {afterInvariant} proves the run actually exercised the system. A
  15 |     | ///         campaign that never minted, never redeemed and never settled would
  16 |     | ///         satisfy every predicate below vacuously, and report the same green as
  17 |     | ///         one that reached every state.
  18 |     | contract InvariantsTest is Test {
  19 |     |     Properties internal props;
  20 |     | 
  21 |     |     function setUp() public {
  22 |     |         props = new Properties();
  23 |     |         targetContract(address(props));
  24 |     |     }
  25 |     | 
  26 |     |     // --- the six predicates, verbatim ---------------------------------------
  27 |     | 
  28 |     |     function invariant_SupplyEqualsSumOfBalances() public view {
  29 |     |         assertTrue(props.echidna_supply_equals_sum_of_balances(), "supply == sum(balances)");
  30 |     |     }
  31 |     | 
  32 |     |     function invariant_UnverifiedNeverHolds() public view {
  33 |     |         assertTrue(props.echidna_unverified_never_holds(), "phantom balance == 0");
  34 |     |     }
  35 |     | 
  36 |     |     function invariant_OracleStampMonotonic() public view {
  37 |     |         assertTrue(props.echidna_oracle_stamp_monotonic(), "oracle stamp monotonic");
  38 |     |     }
  39 |     | 
  40 |     |     function invariant_SupplyConserved() public view {
  41 |     |         assertTrue(props.echidna_supply_conserved(), "minted - burned == totalSupply");
  42 |     |     }
  43 |     | 
  44 |     |     function invariant_RedemptionLedgerConsistent() public view {
  45 |     |         assertTrue(props.echidna_redemption_ledger_consistent(), "redemption ledger consistent");
  46 |     |     }
  47 |     | 
  48 |     |     function invariant_RedemptionRequiresActiveAsset() public view {
  49 |     |         assertTrue(props.echidna_redemption_requires_active_asset(), "redeemed against an inactive asset");
  50 |     |     }
  51 |     | 
  52 |     |     // --- the harness's own declaration --------------------------------------
  53 |     | 
  54 |     |     /// @dev The count `scripts/property-count.sh` checks statically, checked again
  55 |     |     ///      here at runtime against the predicates this file actually asserts. The
  56 |     |     ///      pair is what makes "six properties" mean six: the static gate catches
  57 |     |     ///      a miscount, this catches a predicate nobody wired up.
  58 |     |     function test_declaredPropertyCountMatchesThisFile() public view {
  59 |     |         assertEq(props.pigfoxPropertyCount(), 6, "declared property count");
  60 |     |         assertEq(_predicatesDrivenHere(), props.pigfoxPropertyCount(), "predicates asserted by this file");
  61 |     |     }
  62 |     | 
  63 |     |     function test_harnessSaysWhatItProves() public view {
  64 |     |         assertEq(
  65 |     |             props.pigfoxHarnessDescription(),
  66 |     |             "supply conservation, KYC gating, oracle monotonicity, and a gapless redemption ledger"
  67 |     |         );
  68 |     |     }
  69 |     | 
  70 |     |     /// @dev Counted by calling every predicate this file asserts. Deliberately a
  71 |     |     ///      literal list rather than a number: adding an `invariant_` above
  72 |     |     ///      without adding it here leaves the two disagreeing, which is the point.
  73 |     |     function _predicatesDrivenHere() internal view returns (uint256 n) {
  74 |     |         props.echidna_supply_equals_sum_of_balances();
  75 |     |         n++;
  76 |     |         props.echidna_unverified_never_holds();
  77 |     |         n++;
  78 |     |         props.echidna_oracle_stamp_monotonic();
  79 |     |         n++;
  80 |     |         props.echidna_supply_conserved();
  81 |     |         n++;
  82 |     |         props.echidna_redemption_ledger_consistent();
  83 |     |         n++;
  84 |     |         props.echidna_redemption_requires_active_asset();
  85 |     |         n++;
  86 |     |     }
  87 |     | 
  88 |     |     /// @dev Non-inertness guard. `afterInvariant` runs after EVERY sequence, not
  89 |     |     ///      once at the end, so anything asserted here must be something a single
  90 |     |     ///      64-call sequence reliably reaches — otherwise the guard is a coin
  91 |     |     ///      flip dressed up as a gate.
  92 |     |     ///
  93 |     |     ///      Minting and redeeming qualify: three of the ten entry points drive a
  94 |     |     ///      redemption (`redeem`, `redeemFromActiveAsset`, and `settle`'s
  95 |     |     ///      bootstrap), so a sequence that reaches none of them is a 1-in-10^10
  96 |     |     ///      event. Settlement does NOT qualify — only `settle` produces one, and
  97 |     |     ///      a sequence missing it entirely turned up in roughly one campaign in
  98 |     |     ///      four. That is asserted deterministically by
  99 |     |     ///      {test_settlementLedgerEndToEnd} instead, which is a stronger check
 100 |     |     ///      than a probabilistic one anyway: it pins the double-settle refusal,
 101 |     |     ///      which a fuzz campaign only reaches by luck.
 102 |     |     function afterInvariant() public view {
 103 |     |         assertGt(props.ghostMintsView(), 0, "harness never minted - invariants vacuous");
 104 |     |         assertGt(props.ghostBurnsView(), 0, "harness never redeemed - ledger invariants vacuous");
 105 |     |         assertGt(props.ghostRedeemedTotalView(), 0, "harness redeemed zero tokens");
 106 |     |     }
 107 |     | 
 108 |     |     // --- the settlement path, driven deterministically -----------------------
 109 |     | 
 110 |     |     /// @dev What `afterInvariant` cannot reliably assert, asserted directly: a
 111 |     |     ///      request settles exactly once, a second settlement is refused, and the
 112 |     |     ///      harness's ledger checks stay clean throughout.
 113 |     |     function test_settlementLedgerEndToEnd() public {
 114 |     |         Properties p = new Properties();
 115 |     | 
 116 |     |         p.registerAsset(1);
 117 |     |         p.mintToHolder(0, 1_000 ether);
 118 |     |         p.redeemFromActiveAsset(0, 100 ether);
 119 |     |         assertEq(p.ghostBurnsView(), 1, "one redemption recorded");
 120 |     |         assertGt(p.ghostRedeemedTotalView(), 0, "a non-zero amount was redeemed");
 121 |     |         assertEq(p.ghostSettlementsView(), 0, "nothing settled yet");
 122 |     | 
 123 |     |         p.settle(0);
 124 |     |         assertEq(p.ghostSettlementsView(), 1, "request settled");
 125 |     | 
 126 |     |         // Settling the same request again must be refused. The harness routes
 127 |     |         // that through a try/catch and trips `ledgerInconsistent` if it succeeds,
 128 |     |         // so a silent double-settlement fails here rather than passing quietly.
 129 |     |         p.settle(0);
 130 |     |         assertEq(p.ghostSettlementsView(), 1, "a second settlement must not count");
 131 |     | 
 132 |     |         assertTrue(p.echidna_redemption_ledger_consistent(), "ledger consistent");
 133 |     |         assertTrue(p.echidna_supply_conserved(), "supply conserved");
 134 |     |         assertTrue(p.echidna_redemption_requires_active_asset(), "asset gating held");
 135 |     |     }
 136 |     | 
 137 |     |     /// @dev The guard the whole redemption path rests on: a suspended asset
 138 |     |     ///      cannot back a redemption. Driven directly rather than waiting for the
 139 |     |     ///      fuzzer to suspend an asset and then redeem against that exact id.
 140 |     |     function test_suspendedAssetCannotBeRedeemedAgainst() public {
 141 |     |         Properties p = new Properties();
 142 |     | 
 143 |     |         p.registerAsset(7);
 144 |     |         p.mintToHolder(1, 1_000 ether);
 145 |     |         // Status 2 is Suspended: setAssetStatus maps 1..3 onto Active, Suspended,
 146 |     |         // Redeemed, and the argument is taken modulo 3.
 147 |     |         p.setAssetStatus(0, 1);
 148 |     | 
 149 |     |         uint256 burnsBefore = p.ghostBurnsView();
 150 |     |         p.redeem(1, 0, 100 ether); // asset 0, now suspended
 151 |     |         assertEq(p.ghostBurnsView(), burnsBefore, "a suspended asset must not back a redemption");
 152 |     |         assertTrue(p.echidna_redemption_requires_active_asset(), "asset gating held");
 153 |     |         assertTrue(p.echidna_redemption_ledger_consistent(), "refusal is not a ledger fault");
 154 |     |     }
 155 |     | }

/tmp/codex-phase32-rwa/test/Properties.sol
   1 |     | // SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
   2 |     | pragma solidity 0.8.28;
   3 |     | 
   4 |     | import {PigfoxProperties} from "pipeline/PigfoxProperties.sol";
   5 |     | 
   6 |     | import {AssetRegistry} from "../src/AssetRegistry.sol";
   7 |     | import {IdentityRegistry} from "../src/IdentityRegistry.sol";
   8 |     | import {PriceOracle} from "../src/PriceOracle.sol";
   9 |     | import {Redemption} from "../src/Redemption.sol";
  10 |     | import {RWAToken} from "../src/RWAToken.sol";
  11 |     | 
  12 |     | import {Actor} from "./Actor.sol";
  13 |     | 
  14 |     | /// @title Properties — the RWA system's invariants, in one place.
  15 |     | /// @notice A single property harness driven by all three engines: Foundry's
  16 |     | ///         invariant runner (via {InvariantsTest}), Echidna and Medusa. It
  17 |     | ///         deploys the whole system, holds the owner and agent roles, and exposes
  18 |     | ///         action functions the fuzzers call plus the `echidna_*` predicates.
  19 |     | ///
  20 |     | /// @dev    THE HARNESS COVERS ALL FIVE CONTRACTS, not three. An earlier version
  21 |     | ///         fuzzed the token, the identity registry and the oracle, and left
  22 |     | ///         `AssetRegistry` and `Redemption` to unit tests alone — which meant the
  23 |     | ///         redemption ledger, the part of this system that actually destroys
  24 |     | ///         value, had no invariant on it at all.
  25 |     | ///
  26 |     | /// @dev    WHY THERE ARE ACTOR CONTRACTS.
  27 |     | ///         `Redemption.requestRedemption` records `msg.sender` as the holder and
  28 |     | ///         burns that account's tokens. Neither fuzzer has cheatcodes, so the
  29 |     | ///         only way to have a redemption arrive from someone other than the
  30 |     | ///         harness is to own a contract at that address and call through it.
  31 |     | ///         Four actors mean the ledger invariants see four distinct holders
  32 |     | ///         instead of one, which is the difference between testing the ledger and
  33 |     | ///         testing one row of it.
  34 |     | ///
  35 |     | /// @dev    WHY THE LEDGER CHECKS ARE EAGER.
  36 |     | ///         A predicate that walks every request is quadratic over a campaign —
  37 |     | ///         the fuzzer evaluates predicates after every single call — and it
  38 |     | ///         spends the budget re-reading old state instead of reaching new state.
  39 |     | ///         So each entry point verifies its own effect IMMEDIATELY and trips a
  40 |     | ///         sticky flag, and additionally re-verifies ONE older request
  41 |     | ///         round-robin. Predicates then read the flags in O(1). The comparison
  42 |     | ///         happens at the moment of divergence, on the input that caused it.
  43 |     | ///
  44 |     | /// @dev    `PHANTOM` is deliberately never KYC-verified: no action can ever give
  45 |     | ///         it a balance, which is the transfer-hook invariant made concrete.
  46 | *   | contract Properties is PigfoxProperties {
  47 |     |     AssetRegistry internal immutable ASSETS;
  48 |     |     IdentityRegistry internal immutable IDENTITY;
  49 |     |     PriceOracle internal immutable ORACLE;
  50 |     |     Redemption internal immutable REDEMPTION;
  51 |     |     RWAToken internal immutable TOKEN;
  52 |     | 
  53 | *   |     uint256 internal constant NUM_HOLDERS = 4;
  54 |     |     /// @notice The one address that is never KYC-verified.
  55 |     |     address internal constant PHANTOM = address(0xBAD);
  56 |     | 
  57 |     |     Actor[NUM_HOLDERS] internal actors;
  58 |     |     address[NUM_HOLDERS] internal holders;
  59 |     |     mapping(address => bool) internal isHolder;
  60 |     | 
  61 |     |     // --- ghost state ---------------------------------------------------------

  64 |     |

 244 |     |     /// @notice A holder redeems against an asset that IS Active.
 245 |     |     /// @dev    Guarantees the redemption ledger is actually exercised. Without it
 246 |     |     ///         a sequence has to land `registerAsset`, `mintToHolder` and `redeem`
 247 |     |     ///         in the right order, against an asset nothing has since suspended,
 248 |     |     ///         before a single request exists — and most sequences never do.
 249 | *   |     function redeemFromActiveAsset(uint256 who, uint256 amount) public {
 250 | *   |         uint256 assetId = _anActiveAsset();
 251 | *   |         _redeemAgainst(who % NUM_HOLDERS, assetId, amount);
 252 |     |     }
 253 |     | 
 254 |     |     /// @dev The shared redemption path. The outcome is compared against what the
 255 |     |     ///      harness independently expected: it knows the balance and whether the
 256 |     |     ///      asset was active, so it knows whether the call ought to have
 257 |     |     ///      succeeded.
 258 | *   |     function _redeemAgainst(uint256 index, uint256 assetId, uint256 amount) internal {
 259 | *   |         address holder = holders[index];
 260 |     | 
 261 | *   |         uint256 bal = _ensureHolderHasTokens(holder, amount);
 262 | *   |         amount = 1 + (amount % bal); // 1..bal — zero is rejected by design
 263 |     | 
 264 | *   |         bool wasActive = ASSETS.isActive(assetId);
 265 | *   |         uint256 idBefore = REDEMPTION.requestCount();
 266 | *   |         uint256 supplyBefore = TOKEN.totalSupply();
 267 |     | 
 268 | *   |         (bool ok,) = actors[index]
 269 | *   |         .call(address(REDEMPTION), abi.encodeCall(Redemption.requestRedemption, (assetId, amount)));
 270 |     | 
 271 | *   |         if (ok && !wasActive) {
 272 |     |             // The claim the whole redemption path rests on: value is only ever
 273 |     |             // destroyed against an asset the registrar has marked Active.
 274 |     |             inactiveAssetRedeemed = true;
 275 |     |         }
 276 |     | 
 277 | *   |         if (!ok) {
 278 |     |             // A redemption the harness expected to succeed did not. Nothing about
 279 |     |             // this call could legitimately fail: the asset was active, the holder
 280 |     |             // held the balance, and the amount is non-zero.
 281 | *   |             if (wasActive) ledgerInconsistent = true;
 282 | *   |             _afterCall();
 283 | *   |             return;
 284 |     |         }
 285 |     | 
 286 | *   |         ghostBurns++;
 287 | *   |         ghostBurnedTotal += amount;
 288 | *   |         ghostRedeemedTotal += amount;
 289 |     | 
 290 | *   |         expectedHolder[idBefore] = holder;
 291 | *   |         expectedAmount[idBefore] = amount;
 292 | *   |         expectedAsset[idBefore] = assetId;
 293 | *   |         expectedSettled[idBefore] = false;
 294 |     | 
 295 | *   |         if (REDEMPTION.requestCount() != idBefore + 1) ledgerInconsistent = true;
 296 | *   |         if (TOKEN.totalSupply() != supplyBefore - amount) ledgerInconsistent = true;
 297 | *   |         _verifyRequest(idBefore);
 298 | *   |         _verifyNoRequestBeyondTheCount();
 299 |     | 
 300 |     |         _afterCall();
 301 |     |     }
 302 |     | 
 303 |     |     /// @notice An agent settles a recorded redemption request.
 304 |     |     /// @dev    Creates one first if none exists, for the same reason
 305 |     |     ///         {redeemFromActiveAsset} exists: a `settle` scheduled before any
 306 |     |     ///         redemption in its sequence would otherwise return without touching
 307 |     |     ///         anything, and whole campaigns would never settle at all.
 308 | *   |     function settle(uint256 which) public {
 309 | *   |         if (REDEMPTION.requestCount() == 0) {
 310 | *   |             _redeemAgainst(which % NUM_HOLDERS, _anActiveAsset(), which);
 311 |     |         }
 312 | *   |         uint256 count = REDEMPTION.requestCount();
 313 | *   |         if (count == 0) return; // the bootstrap redemption was refused; nothing to settle
 314 | *   |         uint256 id = which % count;
 315 |     | 
 316 | *   |         if (expectedSettled[id]) {
 317 |     |             // Already settled: the contract must refuse. A second settlement
 318 |     |             // succeeding would mean the off-chain leg could be claimed twice.
 319 |     |             try REDEMPTION.settleRedemption(id) {
 320 |     |                 ledgerInconsistent = true;
 321 |     |             } catch {
 322 |     |                 // expected
 323 |     |             }
 324 |     |         } else {
 325 | *   |             REDEMPTION.settleRedemption(id);
 326 | *   |             expectedSettled[id] = true;
 327 | *   |             ghostSettlements++;
 328 |     |         }
 329 |     | 
 330 | *   |         _verifyRequest(id);
 331 |     |         _afterCall();
 332 |     |     }

 335 |     |                               PROPERTIES

 337 |     | 
 338 |     |     /// @notice totalSupply always equals the sum of every account's balance.
 339 |     |     function echidna_supply_equals_sum_of_balances() public view returns (bool) {
 340 |     |         uint256 sum = TOKEN.balanceOf(address(this)) + TOKEN.balanceOf(PHANTOM);
 341 |     |         for (uint256 i = 0; i < NUM_HOLDERS; i++) {
 342 |     |             sum += TOKEN.balanceOf(holders[i]);
 343 |     |         }
 344 |     |         return sum == TOKEN.totalSupply();
 345 |     |     }
 346 |     | 
 347 |     |     /// @notice The never-verified PHANTOM can never hold a non-zero balance.
 348 |     |     function echidna_unverified_never_holds() public view returns (bool) {
 349 |     |         return TOKEN.balanceOf(PHANTOM) == 0;
 350 |     |     }
 351 |     | 
 352 |     |     /// @notice The oracle timestamp never moves backwards.
 353 |     |     function echidna_oracle_stamp_monotonic() public view returns (bool) {
 354 |     |         return ORACLE.updatedAt() >= lastOracleStamp;
 355 |     |     }
 356 |     | 
 357 |     |     /// @notice Everything minted, minus everything burned, is the supply.
 358 |     |     /// @dev    Stated against the harness's OWN running totals rather than
 359 |     |     ///         against anything the token reports, so a token that mis-accounts a
 360 |     |     ///         mint or a burn cannot satisfy this by being consistently wrong.
 361 |     |     ///         Burns reach the token only through `Redemption`, so this also
 362 |     |     ///         closes the redemption path.
 363 |     |     function echidna_supply_conserved() public view returns (bool) {
 364 |     |         return ghostMintedTotal - ghostBurnedTotal == TOKEN.totalSupply();
 365 |     |     }
 366 |     | 
 367 |     |     /// @notice The redemption ledger is gapless, sequential, records exactly what
 368 |     |     ///         was asked of it, and never settles the same request twice.
 369 |     |     function echidna_redemption_ledger_consistent() public view returns (bool) {
 370 |     |         return !ledgerInconsistent;
 371 |     |     }
 372 |     | 
 373 |     |     /// @notice Value is only ever destroyed against an Active asset.
 374 |     |     function echidna_redemption_requires_active_asset() public view returns (bool) {
 375 |     |         return !inactiveAssetRedeemed && !assetRegistryInconsistent;
 376 |     |     }

 379 |     |                             NON-INERTNESS VIEWS
 380 |     |     //////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////*/
 381 |     | 
 382 |     |     /// @notice Number of mints the fuzzer has driven; used by the non-inertness guard.
 383 |     |     function ghostMintsView() external view returns (uint256) {
 384 |     |         return ghostMints;
 385 |     |     }
 386 |     | 
 387 |     |     /// @notice Number of transfers the fuzzer has driven.
 388 |     |     function ghostTransfersView() external view returns (uint256) {
 389 |     |         return ghostTransfers;
 390 |     |     }
 391 |     | 
 392 |     |     /// @notice Number of burns the fuzzer has driven, all of them redemptions.
 393 |     |     function ghostBurnsView() external view returns (uint256) {
 394 |     |         return ghostBurns;
 395 |     |     }
 396 |     | 
 397 |     |     /// @notice Number of redemption requests settled.
 398 |     |     function ghostSettlementsView() external view returns (uint256) {
 399 |     |         return ghostSettlements;
 400 |     |     }
 401 |     | 
 402 |     |     /// @notice Total amount redeemed across every request.
 403 |     |     function ghostRedeemedTotalView() external view returns (uint256) {
 404 |     |         return ghostRedeemedTotal;
 405 |     |     }

 407 |     |     /*//////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
 408 |     |                                 HELPERS
 409 |     |     //////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////*/
 410 |     | 
 411 |     |     /// @dev Registers an asset if none exists, and returns the count.
 412 |     |     ///      Bootstrapping preconditions in the harness rather than waiting for the
 413 |     |     ///      fuzzer to stumble into the right order is what keeps the budget on the
 414 |     |     ///      ledger instead of on setup. Every bootstrap write is accounted for in
 415 |     |     ///      the ghost totals exactly as a fuzzer-driven one would be, so nothing
 416 |     |     ///      here can make an invariant true by hiding a mutation from it.
 417 | *   |     function _ensureAnAssetExists() internal returns (uint256 count) {
 418 | *   |         count = ASSETS.assetCount();
 419 | *   |         if (count == 0) {
 420 | *   |             ASSETS.registerAsset(keccak256("bootstrap-asset"), "ipfs://bootstrap");
 421 | *   |             count = 1;
 422 |     |         }
 423 |     |     }
 424 |     | 
 425 |     |     /// @dev Returns an Active asset id, making one Active if none is.
 426 | *   |     function _anActiveAsset() internal returns (uint256) {
 427 | *   |         uint256 count = _ensureAnAssetExists();
 428 | *   |         for (uint256 i = 0; i < count; i++) {
 429 | *   |             if (ASSETS.isActive(i)) return i;
 430 |     |         }
 431 |     |         // Everything has been suspended or redeemed. Reactivating asset zero is a
 432 |     |         // legitimate registrar action, and the alternative — returning early — is
 433 |     |         // how a campaign quietly stops testing the ledger.
 434 |     |         ASSETS.setAssetStatus(0, AssetRegistry.Status.Active);
 435 |     |         return 0;
 436 |     |     }
 437 |     | 
 438 |     |     /// @dev Ensures `holder` has something to redeem, and returns the balance.
 439 | *   |     function _ensureHolderHasTokens(address holder, uint256 seed) internal returns (uint256 bal) {
 440 | *   |         bal = TOKEN.balanceOf(holder);
 441 | *   |         if (bal == 0) {
 442 | *   |             uint256 amount = 1 + _bound(seed);
 443 | *   |             TOKEN.mint(holder, amount);
 444 | *   |             ghostMints++;
 445 | *   |             ghostMintedTotal += amount;
 446 | *   |             bal = amount;
 447 |     |         }
 448 |     |     }
 449 |     | 
 450 |     |     /// @dev Runs after every action: re-verify ONE older request, round-robin.
 451 |     |     ///      O(1) per call, and over a campaign it re-reads every request many
 452 |     |     ///      times, interleaved with writes — which is what would catch a later
 453 |     |     ///      call corrupting an earlier record. Walking the whole ledger in a
 454 |     |     ///      predicate would do the same job quadratically.
 455 | *   |     function _afterCall() internal {
 456 | *   |         uint256 count = REDEMPTION.requestCount();
 457 | *   |         if (count == 0) return;
 458 | *   |         _verifyRequest(requestCursor % count);
 459 | *   |         requestCursor++;
 460 |     |     }
 461 |     | 
 462 |     |     /// @dev Compares the contract's record against what the harness recorded when
 463 |     |     ///      the request was made.
 464 | *   |     function _verifyRequest(uint256 id) internal {
 465 | *   |         try REDEMPTION.getRequest(id) returns (Redemption.Request memory r) {
 466 | *   |             if (
 467 | *   |                 !r.exists || r.holder != expectedHolder[id] || r.amount != expectedAmount[id]
 468 | *   |                     || r.assetId != expectedAsset[id] || r.settled != expectedSettled[id]
 469 | *   |                     || !isHolder[r.holder] || r.amount == 0
 470 |     |             ) {
 471 |     |                 ledgerInconsistent = true;
 472 |     |             }
 473 |     |         } catch {
 474 |     |             // Every id below `requestCount` must exist. A revert here is a gap.
 475 |     |             ledgerInconsistent = true;
 476 |     |         }
 477 |     |     }
 478 |     | 
 479 |     |     /// @dev `requestCount` is also the next id, so nothing may exist at it yet.
 480 |     |     ///      Ids that ran ahead of the counter would break pagination silently.
 481 | *   |     function _verifyNoRequestBeyondTheCount() internal {
 482 | *   |         try REDEMPTION.getRequest(REDEMPTION.requestCount()) returns (Redemption.Request memory) {
 483 |     |             ledgerInconsistent = true;
 484 |     |         } catch {
 485 |     |             // expected
 486 |     |         }
 487 |     |     }
 488 |     | 
 489 | *   |     function _bound(uint256 amount) internal pure returns (uint256) {
 490 |     |         // Keep amounts in a range that can never overflow uint256 supply.
 491 | *   |         return amount % (1_000_000 ether);
 492 |     |     }

  36 |     |     function test_Request_Succeeds() public {
  37 |     |         uint256 assetId = _registerAsset();
  38 |     |         _mint(alice, AMOUNT);
  39 |     | 
  40 |     |         vm.expectEmit(true, true, true, true);
  41 |     |         emit Redemption.RedemptionRequested(0, alice, assetId, 300 ether);
  42 |     |         vm.prank(alice);
  43 |     |         uint256 reqId = redemption.requestRedemption(assetId, 300 ether);
  44 |     | 
  45 |     |         assertEq(reqId, 0, "first request id");
  46 |     |         assertEq(redemption.requestCount(), 1, "count");
  47 |     |         assertEq(token.balanceOf(alice), 700 ether, "tokens burned");
  48 |     |         assertEq(token.totalSupply(), 700 ether, "supply reduced");
  49 |     | 
  50 |     |         Redemption.Request memory r = redemption.getRequest(reqId);
  51 |     |         assertEq(r.holder, alice, "holder");
  52 |     |         assertEq(r.assetId, assetId, "assetId");
  53 |     |         assertEq(r.amount, 300 ether, "amount");
  54 |     |         assertFalse(r.settled, "not settled");
  55 |     |         assertTrue(r.exists, "exists");
  56 |     |     }
  57 |     | 
  58 |     |     function test_Request_RevertsOnZeroAmount() public {
  59 |     |         uint256 assetId = _registerAsset();
  60 |     |         vm.prank(alice);
  61 |     |         vm.expectRevert(Redemption.ZeroAmount.selector);
  62 |     |         redemption.requestRedemption(assetId, 0);
  63 |     |     }
  64 |     | 
  65 |     |     function test_Request_RevertsWhenAssetNotActive() public {
  66 |     |         // no asset registered → id 0 is not active
  67 |     |         _mint(alice, AMOUNT);
  68 |     |         vm.prank(alice);
  69 |     |         vm.expectRevert(abi.encodeWithSelector(Redemption.AssetNotActive.selector, 0));
  70 |     |         redemption.requestRedemption(0, 1 ether);
  71 |     |     }
  72 |     | 
  73 |     |     function test_Request_RevertsWhenHolderLacksBalance() public {

  75 |     |         // alice is verified but holds nothing → token burn reverts
  76 |     |         vm.prank(alice);
  77 |     |         vm.expectRevert(abi.encodeWithSelector(RWAToken.InsufficientBalance.selector, alice, 0, 1 ether));
  78 |     |         redemption.requestRedemption(assetId, 1 ether);
  79 |     |     }

  99 |     | 
 100 |     |     function test_Settle_RevertsWhenAlreadySettled() public {

 103 |     |         redemption.settleRedemption(reqId);
 104 |     |         vm.prank(owner);
 105 |     |         vm.expectRevert(abi.encodeWithSelector(Redemption.AlreadySettled.selector, reqId));
 106 |     |         redemption.settleRedemption(reqId);

 113 |     |         redemption.settleRedemption(reqId);

 119 |     | 
 120 |     |     function test_GetRequest_RevertsOnUnknown() public {

 122 |     |         redemption.getRequest(0);
 123 |     |     }

 130 |     |         uint256 assetId = _registerAsset();
 131 |     |         _mint(alice, AMOUNT);
